output.statement: For coprime integers m,n with n>0, mn≠0, and m²≠n², put H=m²+n², D=m²−n², and Q=m⁴+34m²n²+n⁴. Define a=−9H/(8D), b=(m²−7n²)H(7m²−n²)/(8D³), c=8D³/(9H³), e=−2(m²+5n²)(5m²+n²)/(9DH), f=−2mn(m²−4mn−3n²)(3m²−4mn−n²)(m³+8m²n+5mn²+4n³)(4m³−5m²n+8mn²−n³)/(DHQ²), and g=2mn(m²+4mn−3n²)(3m²+4mn−n²)(m³−8m²n+5mn²−4n³)(4m³+5m²n+8mn²+n³)/(DHQ²). Then none of a,b,c,e,f,g is an integer. Moreover, Q has a prime divisor p>3; every prime p>3 dividing Q satisfies p≡1 (mod 8) and vₚ(f)=vₚ(g)=−2vₚ(Q).
assumptions: m,n are coprime integers with n>0, mn≠0, and m²≠n²; these are the reduced-parameter conditions for rational t outside {0,1,−1}.
H=m²+n², D=m²−n², Q=m⁴+34m²n²+n⁴, and the six rational coordinates are exactly the formulas stated in the lemma statement.
quantifiers: For every pair of integers m,n satisfying the assumptions, with no height bound.
For every prime p>3 dividing the corresponding positive integer Q.
output.objective: Prove the stated nonintegrality and prime-divisor assertions for the displayed rational family.
output.proof:
All valuations below are normalized so that v_p(p)=1. Since gcd(m,n)=1, either m,n have opposite parity or both are odd. Neither m²−7n² nor 7m²−n² vanishes: either equality would imply that 7 or 1/7 is a rational square, impossible by comparing the exponent of 7 in a reduced numerator-denominator equation.

If m,n have opposite parity, H,D,m²−7n², and 7m²−n² are odd. Thus v₂(a)=v₂(b)=−3. If both are odd, then v₂(H)=1 and v₂(D)≥3, since odd squares are 1 modulo 8. Also m²−7n²≡2 (mod 8) and 7m²−n²≡6 (mod 8), so each has 2-adic valuation 1. Consequently v₂(a)=1−3−v₂(D)<0 and v₂(b)=1+1+1−3−3v₂(D)=−3v₂(D)<0. Thus a and b are nonintegers in either case. Further, H+D=2m² and H−D=2n² are positive, so 0<|D|<H. Hence 0<|c|=(8/9)(|D|/H)³<8/9, proving c is not an integer.

Write the numerator of e as N=−2(m²+5n²)(5m²+n²). If e were an integer, H would divide N. Modulo H, m²≡−n², so N≡32n⁴ (mod H). Since gcd(H,n)=1, this would imply H|32. But H has 2-adic valuation 0 when m,n have opposite parity and 1 when both are odd. A positive divisor of 32 with either valuation is 1 or 2. In contrast, m,n are nonzero and |m|≠n, so H=m²+n²≥5. This contradiction proves e is not an integer.

The integer Q is positive. If m,n have opposite parity, Q is odd; if both are odd, m⁴≡n⁴≡1 (mod 16) and m²n²≡1 or 9 (mod 16), whence Q≡4 (mod 16). Therefore v₂(Q) is 0 or 2. If 3|mn, coprimality gives Q≡1 (mod 3). Otherwise m²≡n²≡1 (mod 3), and D=3k for some integer k. The identity Q=D²+36m²n² gives Q=9(k²+4m²n²); the factor in parentheses is nonzero modulo 3 because k² is 0 or 1 modulo 3 and 4m²n²≡1 modulo 3. Thus v₃(Q) is 0 or 2. If Q had no prime divisor greater than 3, these valuation bounds would give Q|36. But the distinct positive integers |m| and n have squared sum at least 5, and their squares have product at least 4. Hence Q=m⁴+n⁴+34m²n²≥16+1+136=153, contradicting Q|36. So some prime p>3 divides Q.

Fix any prime p>3 dividing Q. No prime dividing Q can divide m or n: reducing Q modulo such a prime would leave the fourth power of the other integer, which is nonzero by coprimality. Also Q=D²+36m²n² and Q=H²+32m²n² show that p divides neither D nor H.

For explicit noncancellation certificates, let q(T)=T⁴+34T²+1 and let P₁=T²−4T−3, P₂=3T²−4T−1, P₃=T³+8T²+5T+4, P₄=4T³−5T²+8T−1. Direct multiplication gives the identities
q+(-T³−34T)T=1,
(33−7T)q+(7T³−5T²+239T−181)P₁=576,
(197−123T)q+(41T³−11T²+1393T−379)P₂=576,
(17T²+123T−20)q+(-17T³+13T²−577T+437)P₃=1728,
(628T²−717T+1151)q+(-157T³−17T²−5333T−577)P₄=1728.
These are polynomial identities over the integers, verified by multiplying the displayed factors and collecting coefficients. In F_p, T=m/n is defined and q(T)=Q/n⁴=0. Since p>3, 576 and 1728 are nonzero modulo p, and the identities imply Pᵢ(T)≠0 for each i. Also T≠0. Homogenizing each Pᵢ multiplies its value by n² or n³, a unit modulo p. Thus all four corresponding polynomial factors in the numerator of f, as well as mn, are nonzero modulo p. The numerator of f is therefore a p-adic unit. Its denominator has valuation 2v_p(Q), since p∤DH. This proves v_p(f)=−2v_p(Q)<0, so f is not an integer.

Substitution gives g(m,n)=f(−m,n): the two quadratic factors become those in g, the prefactor changes sign, and each cubic factor changes to the negative of its counterpart, so their two sign changes cancel. The hypotheses still hold for (−m,n), and H,D,Q are unchanged. Applying the same argument at p to this pair proves v_p(g)=−2v_p(Q)<0. This proves g is not an integer and establishes the asserted valuations for every p>3 dividing Q.

It remains to prove the congruence for such a prime p. In F_p define r=D/(6mn) and s=H/(4mn); their denominators are units. From the two identities for Q above and p|Q, we obtain r²=−1 and s²=−2. Set u=s/r and z=u(1+r)/2. Then u²=2 and
z²=2(1+2r+r²)/4=r,
so z⁴=−1. Since p is odd, −1≠1 in F_p, and z has order exactly 8 in F_p*. By Lagrange's theorem the order divides |F_p*|=p−1, hence p≡1 (mod 8). This completes all claims for the stated family.
output.method_summary: Use parity valuations and a size bound for a,b,c,e; establish a prime p>3 dividing Q via exact 2-adic and 3-adic bounds; give explicit polynomial Bezout identities preventing numerator cancellation modulo every such p; then use an order-eight element in F_p* to prove p≡1 mod 8.
